headline: Growth accelerates as full-year guidance is raised
summary_short: Gen Digital's fiscal Q1 2027 (our calendar-quarter label: FY2026 Q2) revenue rose 6.3% year-over-year to $1,336 million, with GAAP diluted EPS up 63.6% to $0.36 and non-GAAP diluted EPS at $0.71; the company beat its own guidance and raised full-year non-GAAP revenue and EPS guidance.
summary_long: Revenue grew 6.3% y/y to $1,336M (+11% on the company's own non-GAAP comparable basis, excluding Q1 FY26's extra reporting week and including MoneyLion's prior-year stub). GAAP operating income was roughly flat at $443M as higher restructuring ($32M vs $10M) and litigation costs ($23M vs $5M) offset gross-margin gains; non-GAAP operating income rose 9% to $668M. Net income rose 59.3% to $215M on lower interest expense and a smaller tax provision, lifting GAAP diluted EPS 63.6% to $0.36; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.71. Operating cash flow rose 6.1% to $434M; cash grew to $564M from $411M. Gen initiated Q2 FY2027 guidance ($1.325-1.350B revenue / $0.71-0.73 non-GAAP EPS) and raised full-year FY2027 non-GAAP guidance to $5.375-5.475B revenue / $2.87-2.97 EPS.

Fiscal-offset note: Gen Digital's own release labels this quarter "Q1 Fiscal Year 2027" (13 weeks ended July 3, 2026); our shard's calendar-derived label for the same report is "FY2026 Q2" — same underlying quarter, different fiscal-year numbering convention (Gen's fiscal year runs roughly April-March). Comparability quirk: the year-ago quarter (Q1 FY2026) had an extra (14th) reporting week and did not yet include a full quarter of MoneyLion (acquired mid-quarter), so the company's own headline growth-rate claims ("revenue up 11%", "non-GAAP diluted EPS up 19%") are computed on its own comparable/adjusted basis, which differs from the straight GAAP-to-GAAP and non-GAAP-to-non-GAAP percentages computed here from the reported dollar figures. GAAP vs non-GAAP diluted EPS ($0.36 vs $0.71) diverges due to stock-based compensation, amortization of acquisition intangibles, restructuring, litigation costs, and non-cash interest expense add-backs, per the release's own reconciliation table.

drivers.explanation: Growth was broad-based across segments: Trust-Based Solutions (identity, financial wellness) revenue rose to $490M from $388M, while Cyber Safety Platform revenue slipped to $846M from $869M, per the release's segment breakout.
Held back by higher restructuring and other costs ($32M vs $10M a year ago) and higher litigation costs ($23M vs $5M), which offset gross-margin improvement from revenue growth.
Growth reflects lower interest expense ($124M vs $156M, from debt paydown) and a smaller income-tax provision ($108M vs $165M), on top of flat operating income.
Tracks net-income growth plus a smaller diluted share count (603M vs 624M) from ongoing buybacks ($100M repurchased this quarter).
Management called it a "beat-and-raise start to fiscal 2027," citing broad-based platform strength and raising full-year non-GAAP revenue and EPS guidance on the back of the Q1 beat.
